parole.significato: A member of an Amerindian people who lived in the region of the Caribbean when the Spanish arrived in America.
parole.testo: From Kari'na Aruwako, from the name in Lokono.

parole.significato: A thick black liquid made from cassava root and spices, used medicinally and as a flavouring and preservative.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Kari'na kasirìpo, perhaps by way of some intermediary language.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Kari'na kasiri, both directly and by way of intermediaries such as Portuguese caxiri.

Any of the family Tayassuidae of mammals from the Americas, related to pigs.
parole.testo: From Kari'na pakira (“collared peccary”), from Proto-Cariban *pakira.

parole.significato: Any tree of the genus Caryocar. They yield strong timber and some bear edible nuts.
parole.testo: From Kari'na sawari, via Caribbean French saouari. Attested in English (as souwarrow or saoari) from the 19th century.

parole.significato: Any member of the avian family Tinamidae of tinamous.

parole.testo: Derived from Kari'na tamali /tumale (“a sauce of lobster liver”).

parole.significato: Any of several evergreen plants of the genus Yucca, having long, pointed, and rigid leaves at the top of a woody stem,…
parole.testo: Variant of yuca, sometimes said to be from Kari'na yuca (“cassava (Manihot esculenta)”), but this latter appears to be a ghost word. The word was applied to plants of the genus Yucca (now the main sense), because Carl Linnaeus (1707–1778) and others confused them with the cassava.

parole.significato: The andiroba or crabwood tree (Carapa guianensis).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Trinidadian Creole English crappo, crapaud, a modification of either Lokono carapa, kálaba, karaba, or Kari'na karapa. Cognates * Dutch krapboom * Sranan Tongo krapa

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Nicotiana.
